title: Pelvic Support Anatomy: Ligaments, Fascia & Levator Ani
description: Understand pelvic support anatomy, examining the levator ani muscular dome, cardinal and uterosacral ligaments, endopelvic fascial planes, and pelvic body.
h1: Female Pelvic Support Anatomy: Ligaments, Endopelvic Fascia and Floor
blurb: How the tonic levator ani muscular dome, cardinal and uterosacral ligaments, and endopelvic fascial planes suspend pelvic organs above the urogenital hiatus.
lead: Pelvic organs stay suspended over the urogenital opening thanks to a two-part engineering system: a tonic muscular trampoline below and fibrous fascial tethers above. In this illustrated guide to pelvic support ligaments and fascia, we examine 20 documented structures—including broad ligament, mesometrium, mesosalpinx, mesovarium—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Pelvic organs stay suspended over the urogenital opening thanks to a two-part engineering system: a tonic muscular trampoline below and fibrous fascial tethers above. Study true support separately from peritoneal reflections. This realistic pelvis plate shows why the ureter and arteries demand a careful surgical plane. Within the human body, the pelvic support & surgical planes (Fascia et ligamenta pelvis feminae) is situated in uterus, sidewall and pelvic floor, receives arterial perfusion via uterine / ovarian / vaginal / internal pudendal vessels, and is innervated by inferior hypogastric plexus + pudendal nerve.

The broad ligament (Ligamentum latum uteri) is double peritoneal sheet draped over uterus, tubes and associated structures. Physiologically, the broad ligament supports relationships but is not the main mechanical uterine support. Structurally, the mesometrium comprises largest sheet of broad ligament lateral to uterus. Physiologically, the mesometrium governs conveys uterine vessels and connective tissue in base. The mesosalpinx is broad ligament portion related to uterine tube. Physiologically, the mesosalpinx supports tube and its vessels. The mesovarium is short fold suspending ovarian hilum from posterior broad ligament. Physiologically, the mesovarium transmits vessels to ovary. Structurally, the round ligament (Ligamentum teres uteri) comprises band from uterine cornu through inguinal canal to labium majus. Physiologically, the round ligament helps maintain anteversion; not principal apical support. Structurally, the ovarian ligament (Ligamentum ovarii proprium) comprises cornu-to-ovary band medial to ovarian hilum. Physiologically, the ovarian ligament anchors ovary toward uterus.

Clinically, regarding the broad ligament, ureter and uterine vessels course at its base. From a diagnostic standpoint, in the mesometrium, surgical dissection exposes adjacent ureter. In clinical pathology involving the mesosalpinx, tubal surgery separates this vascular fold. Medical evaluation of the mesovarium also notes that distinct from the suspensory ovarian ligament.

questions.question: What is the difference between the broad ligament and pelvic support ligaments?
questions.answer: The broad ligament is a peritoneal fold. Cardinal and uterosacral connective tissues, together with pelvic-floor muscles, contribute substantially to uterine support. Structurally, the cardinal ligament (Ligamentum cardinale) comprises transverse cervical connective tissue to pelvic sidewall. Physiologically, the cardinal ligament governs important apical support with uterine artery/vein.

questions.question: Why is the ureter important in pelvic surgery anatomy?
questions.answer: The ureter travels near the uterine artery and cervix. Understanding their relationship helps explain why surgical planes require careful identification. The distal ureter (Ureter) runs along pelvic sidewall then beneath uterine artery near cervix. Physiologically, the distal ureter delivers urine to bladder.

questions.question: What is the broad ligament?
questions.answer: Double peritoneal sheet draped over uterus, tubes and associated structures. Functionally, it supports relationships but is not the main mechanical uterine support. In clinical pathology involving the broad ligament, ureter and uterine vessels course at its base.

questions.question: Where is the mesosalpinx located?
questions.answer: Broad ligament portion related to uterine tube. Functionally, it supports tube and its vessels. Medical evaluation of the mesosalpinx also notes that tubal surgery separates this vascular fold.

questions.question: What is the function of the round ligament?
questions.answer: Functionally, it helps maintain anteversion; not principal apical support. Band from uterine cornu through inguinal canal to labium majus. Clinically, regarding the round ligament, relevant to round-ligament pain and inguinal surgery.
